question: What oxygen levels did the Saffire-II tests cover, and did any reach the lunar habitat level of 30%?
claim: The 9 Saffire-II (PSI-99) tests covered oxygen levels from 21.5% to 22.1% O2, and none of them (0 of 9) reached the 30% lunar habitat level.
summary_student: Saffire-II burned 9 samples of solid materials in microgravity, and the air around them held between 21.5% and 22.1% oxygen, close to ordinary Earth air. None of the 9 tests reached the 30% oxygen of a lunar habitat, so these results cannot tell us directly how these materials would burn at that level.
summary_professional: PSI-99 (SAFFIRE-II) reports 9 microgravity solid-fuel tests (silicone, cotton-fiberglass SIBAL, PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex) with O2 ranging from 21.5% to 22.1% across all rows (o2_pct_min to o2_pct_max). 0 of 9 tests were at or above the 30% O2 threshold of the lunar base atmosphere. The source table gives no ambient pressure, so the pressure side of the lunar atmosphere cannot be compared.

method.formula: For each investigation, the lowest and highest oxygen percentage over its tests that report oxygen, the number of those tests, and how many reached at least threshold_pct (o2_pct_max >= threshold_pct).

assumptions: Oxygen is read from the Percent O2 column of the Saffire-II table; a note in the table says it was derived from measured CO2 production, and several cells are approximate (marked ~) or given as ranges.
For cells that give a range, the lowest and highest values of the cell are used as o2_pct_min and o2_pct_max.
Mole fraction and volume fraction of O2 are treated as equal (ideal gas).
The lunar habitat level is the 30% O2 threshold given in the question and in _config/environments.md.
limitations: This finding covers only PSI-99 (Saffire-II); it does not include Saffire-I, Saffire-III, BASS, BASS-II or other solid-fuel investigations, which may have tested other oxygen levels.
All Saffire-II tests are in microgravity; the finding says nothing about burning behavior in lunar gravity.
The Saffire-II table gives no ambient pressure, so these tests cannot be checked against the lunar base pressure limit.
No test at 30% O2 means no data at that level, not that these materials are safe or unsafe there; results near Earth-air oxygen must not be extrapolated to 30% O2.
Some rows have an empty material cell in the source table (possibly merged cells), so this finding does not assign a material to those rows.
warnings: PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data. Lunar and Mars conclusions are bounded by microgravity and Earth-gravity results only.

chart.idea: A range bar of the oxygen levels tested by Saffire-II, with a dashed line at the 30% lunar habitat level.

visual_offer.footnote: Want a visual? I can draw a chart of the Saffire-II oxygen range against the 30% lunar habitat level.
